drafts.draft_en: Haunted (1972). A fake 70s horror trailer, every frame AI, film grain and all. This Saturday's Challenge: make your own retro Halloween trailer. Workflow + prompt below 👇
drafts.video_tip: 15s faux 1972 horror trailer: 4:3, heavy grain, gate weave, faded Ektachrome palette, 3 quick shots (foggy house, slow push on a face, lantern in a corridor) ending on a title card 'HAUNTED (1972)'. Post the prompt in the first reply.

drafts.draft_en: Magnific Move just dropped, so I threw a real VFX shot at it: one still plate, three camera moves, zero roto. Here's what worked and what broke 🧵
drafts.video_tip: Split screen: the original still on the left, the Magnific Move result on the right, cycling through 3 camera moves (dolly in, orbit, crane up). End with one failure case to build trust.

drafts.draft_en: Storyboard in, finished shot out. Seedance 2.5 turned 6 rough sketches into a continuous 3D sequence in minutes. Sketch vs. final below 👇
drafts.video_tip: Wipe transition from each pencil storyboard panel to its rendered 3D shot, 6 panels in 12s, same framing on both sides so the match reads instantly.

drafts.draft_en: Body doubles just got an upgrade. A pianist plays, Seedance 2.5 swaps in my character, the hands stay real. VFX supervisors, would you ship this?
drafts.video_tip: Before/after v2v of a real performance (hands on keys or a dance move), source on top, swapped character below, synced, 10s. Freeze on a close-up of the hands at the end.

drafts.draft_en: One Canvas, one Halloween short. Characters, sets and shots all came from a single Firefly board before I touched video. Breakdown below 🎃👇
drafts.video_tip: Zoom out from the final shot to reveal the whole canvas board (characters, sets, keyframes), then cut back into a 10s spooky sequence built from it.
